text:
Maya R.: quick RFC follow-up — re the alloc ABI simplification: I sketched a minimal handoff API to unify offload vs resident paths. want early eyeballs before i turn it into a PR.

Maya R.: current problem: many callers assume "free(ptr)" is cheap and synchronous. once we introduce async handoff (staged offload -> nvme/host), frees can block or require callback. leads to tail p99 stalls for small requests.

Maya R.: proposed tiny API:
```
// minimal allocator handoff contract
allocate(size, flags) -> ptr
free(ptr) -> status   // status: OK | ASYNC_PENDING | ERROR
wait_free(ptr, timeout_ms) -> bool
handoff_notify(ptr, reason) // optional hook used by runtime
```

Sam K.: looks sensible. main tradeoff is on callers: either check ASYNC_PENDING or call wait_free. we should avoid changing hot paths in runtime request path.

Priya V.: agree. can we encode flags to request sync free (for tight-latency paths) vs best-effort offload? e.g., flags = {SYNC_FREE, ALLOW_STAGING}.

Maya R.: yep, intended. default is ALLOW_STAGING. SYNC_FREE would block and cost latency but preserve current semantics for small allocations used during token generation.

Alex G.: a couple infra concerns: 1) how does this interact with eviction coordinator & KV cache? if frees become async, KV cache could keep stale pointer references. need clear ownership transfer points. 2) rolling deploy: older hosts won't implement wait_free/handoff_notify — compat shim needed.

Maya R.: good calls. plan: implement compatibility layer where free() returns OK on old nodes and runtime treats that as implicit sync. new nodes can return ASYNC_PENDING and emit a short-lived token.

Sarah (eng-sre): telemetry we need: histogram of free latency (inc p50/p95/p99), count of ASYNC_PENDING frees, and a gauge for outstanding staged pages per host. also alarm if staged-pages > X for > Y minutes.

Priya V.: fragmentation angle: by delaying reclamation we risk more intra-tenant fragmentation. maybe handoff should return a frag-hint (size bin) so allocator can coalesce later.

Maya R.: thinking of returning metadata: status + frag_hint. frag_hint is optional small int e.g., 64/128/256. should be cheap.

Sam K.: another risk: recompute vs prefetch. when a page is demoted we might choose to recompute rather than bring back from host. handoff_notify should allow a lifecycle state so caller can decide: RECOMPUTE_OK vs MUST_RESTORE.

Alex G.: deployment plan suggestion: feature-flag the new ABI, first behind canary pool, run for 72h with synthetic workload (burst + microbatch) and watch p99 for infer and staged-pages. fallback toggle must be fast.

Maya R.: +1. I'll draft rollout steps in PR: feature flag, canary, broaden, then final removal of old shim after 2 weeks of stable metrics.

Sarah (eng-sre): sample alert rule:
```
if (staged_pages_count > 1000 && staged_pages_age_median > 300s) -> SEV2
if (free_latency_p99 increases by > 50% from baseline) -> paging-triage channel ping
```

Priya V.: question about Dedicated vs Hosted: some customers on Dedicated may want strict sync semantics for compliance. we need tenant-level config to force SYNC_FREE for those pins.

Maya R.: agreed, add tenant-level override. defaults keep ALLOW_STAGING.

Sam K.: one more: can we keep a small fast-path in allocator: if size <= 256 and flags includes FAST_PATH, always do immediate free on GPU to avoid token churn for tiny allocs? avoids tail spikes for small tensors.

Maya R.: yes — implement FAST_PATH and make runtime choose it for KV cache and decoder temp buffers.

Alex G.: please include a brief compatibility matrix in the PR: call sites (inference hotpath, batcher, prefetcher) and required changes. saves review time.

Maya R.: will do. I'll post a draft PR tomorrow. thanks all. :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary pool (rack-7) will receive new runtime build at 2026-03-22T03:00Z. monitor channel #release-war-room for alerts.
